title: GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Drives Pre-orders Despite Pricing Debate
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick reveals that many players pre-ordering GTA 6 are opting for the $100 Ultimate edition rather than the $80 standard edition.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Pre-orders: Players Favor the Ultimate Edition

As the gaming community continues to discuss the economics of modern blockbusters, the pricing and purchasing trends for Rockstar Games' upcoming *Grand Theft Auto 6* have taken center stage. While some consumers may balk at the idea of paying triple-digit prices for a single video game, recent disclosures from Take-Two leadership shed new light on actual consumer behavior.

### The Shift Toward Premium Editions

According to Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two, a significant portion of players who have already pre-ordered *Grand Theft Auto 6* are bypassing the $80 (£70) standard edition in favor of the more expensive $100 (£90) Ultimate edition. This revelation challenges the assumption that higher price tiers will face immediate pushback from the core fanbase, highlighting a strong willingness to pay for premium packages among eager players.

### Market Implications for AAA Gaming

As development budgets for massive open-world titles continue to balloon, the industry has slowly shifted its baseline pricing structures. The fact that many early adopters are gravitating toward the most expensive tier of *GTA 6* suggests that elite franchises maintain immense pricing power. Players are clearly demonstrating that they expect exceptional value and are ready to invest in the definitive versions of their most anticipated games.

## Editor's Take
While a $100 price tag for video games sparks necessary debates about accessibility and industry inflation, Take-Two's insights show that *GTA 6* operates in a league of its own. The strong demand for the Ultimate edition proves that for generation-defining titles, dedicated fans are more than willing to pay a premium for the ultimate experience.
